title: tests/db shell scripts run with set -e only, and uv steps are quiet, to keep DB CI logs readable
answers: Why does the database CI log print every shell command or a huge package list?
Should I add set -x to the tests/db entrypoint or compose scripts for debugging?
How do I keep uv output out of the database CI job logs?
Which flags should tests/db shell scripts use so only pytest output and errors show?
body:
Convention: the tests/db scripts use `set -e` (not `set -ex`), so the CI log has no per-command trace lines.
Quiet uv: `uv sync` in tests/db/entrypoint.sh and `uv export` / `uv run` in tests/db/check_migration.sh take `--quiet`, and the export's stdout is sent to `/dev/null`.
The installed-package listing (`uv pip list`) was removed from tests/db/entrypoint.sh, so nothing dumps a dependency list per container.
Compose wrapper tests/db/compose.sh also uses `set -e` only; its `down --volumes` step keeps its output redirected to `/dev/null`.
Pytest output and errors must stay visible: do not add quiet or redirect flags to the test command itself.
Constraint: the trace is removed for CI noise, not for correctness, so if a run fails, re-add `-x` locally rather than committing it.
applies: Shell scripts under tests/db used by the database CI job and its compose stack; not for other CI jobs or the repository's general scripts.
says: Database build logs print every shell command instead of just test failures.
Automated database test runs show massive package lists that drown out errors.
Make database continuous integration logs cleaner so failures are easy to spot.
Hide dependency sync traces from the database test job console output.
Database pipeline run history shows verbose command execution traces during builds.
search: Shell scripts under tests/db (entrypoint.sh, compose.sh, check_migration.sh) use set -e without -x and run uv commands with --quiet or output sent to /dev/null to keep database CI logs readable. Package listings via uv pip list are omitted from entrypoint.sh, and compose wrapper down commands redirect output to /dev/null, while pytest output and errors must stay visible. The trace is removed for CI noise rather than correctness, so -x may be added locally when debugging but must not be committed.
